# Dataset card: ColdChain synthetic fridge telemetry

*Generated by `python -m data.generate` (seed 2026) on 2026-10-18. Every
number here
comes from `dataset_stats.json`; regenerate instead of editing.*

## What it is

10 simulated vaccine fridges × 60 days, sampled every 5 s and stored as 1-minute rows
(862,060 rows). Temperature is above 8 °C in 4.89 % of minutes.

## How it was made

- **Physics:** the simulator's own thermal model (`tools/coldchain_tools/sim_engine.py`, the Python port of
  the firmware): `dT/dt = k_leak(Tamb − T) + door·k_door(Tamb − T) − comp·cool_rate·efficiency`, compressor
  hysteresis 7.0 / 3.0 °C with the 60 s minimum off time, compressor forced off on battery, the battery
  model (2 %/min drain; at 0 % the node goes silent until power returns).
- **Profiles** differ in ambient (24–36 °C), heat leak, door leak, cooling capacity, sensor noise and how busy
  the door is. The ambient also follows a daily cycle (±2.5 °C, warmest mid-afternoon) plus a slow random walk
  that no feature sees directly.
- **Events** (decided up front from the seed, then simulated):
  - door openings follow the working day (08–20 UTC; a tenth of the rate at night); 85 % last 5–60 s and
    15 % last 1–5 min (10,754 in total);
  - the door left ajar for 20–90 min in working hours, about three a week: the switch reads open but
    the compressor almost keeps up, so the temperature creeps up over many minutes (or holds)
    (247 in total);
  - power failures of 5–90 min, about one every 4 days (146 in total);
  - gradual compressor degradation arcs, efficiency 1.0 → 0.30–0.45 over 8–13 days and then a repair
    (22 arcs, at least 3 per degrading profile over 60 days);
  - sudden compressor faults, efficiency 0.15–0.35 for 3–24 h (6 in total);
  - missing segments of 10–90 min where rows are dropped, on top of the silence while a node's battery is
    dead.
- **Storage:** `ml/data/raw/<profile>.csv.gz` with `fridge_profile, ts, temp, door, comp, power, batt,
  efficiency_true, ambient_true`. `door` and `comp` are the fraction of the minute open / running, `power` is
  1 when on battery, `temp` the minute mean. The 5 s → 1 min step is `features.to_minutes`, the function
  the serving API uses on live readings.
- `efficiency_true` and `ambient_true` are **labels only**: the feature functions never receive them.

## Labels

- `y_temp_h`: the temperature h = 5, 10, 20, 30 minutes after `t` (missing when that
  minute is).
- `y_breach_30`: whether the maximum temperature over `(t, t + 30 min]` is above 8 °C; missing when fewer than
  20 of those minutes exist (for example while a dead node is silent).
- `y_health`: `100 × efficiency_true`, clipped to [0, 100].

## Features

- **Forecast** (42, `features.FEATURES`): from the 60 minutes ending at `t`. Temperature
  (current; mean, std, min and max over 5/15/30/60 min; slopes over 5/15/30 min; acceleration), door (fraction
  open over 5/15/60 min, time since the last opening, current open duration), compressor (on now, duty over
  15/60 min, time since last ON / OFF, current run, switches in 60 min), power (on battery, battery minutes in
  60 min, battery %), derived (time to 8 °C at the current slope, minimum-off wait), missing fraction and
  hour of
  day.
- **Compressor health** (15, `features.HEALTH_FEATURES`): from the 24 hours
  ending at
  `t`, door and battery minutes left out. Cooling rate while ON, warming rate while OFF, mean ON / OFF
  durations, 7 → 3 °C pull-down time, overshoot above 7 °C after switching on, cycles per hour, duty cycle and
  its trend, longest ON run, mean / max temperature and time above 8 °C.

`temp_now, minutes_since_reading, temp_mean_5, temp_std_5, …` and `cool_rate_on, warm_rate_off, on_duration_mean, off_duration_mean, …` are the column orders the models
and the
API share.

## Splits

Never shuffled. Held-out profiles (city-depot, mobile-unit) are test only. On the other
profiles the last 10 days are test, the 10 before them validation, the rest training. Rows near each boundary
are marked `gap` and not used: a training label must not reach into validation time, and a validation window
must not reach back into training labels (30 + 60 min for forecasts, 24 h for health).

| Split | Forecast rows | Breach rows | Breach rate (natural) | Health rows |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| train | 91,786 | 10,208 | 11.1 % | 7,612 |
| val | 22,827 | 2,694 | 11.8 % | 1,723 |
| test | 57,389 | 4,301 | 7.5 % | 4,586 |
| gap | 288 | 0 | 0.0 % | 383 |

Breaches are rare. Evaluation keeps the natural ratio; any rebalancing happens in training only.

## Limitations

- **Synthetic.** The data comes from the same family of physics as the simulator that drives the demo. A model
  trained on it will look better than it would on a real fridge. Real fridges differ: non-linear compressors,
  defrost cycles, load mass, sensor placement and drift.
- The disturbances (ambient drift, noise, faults, missing data) are there so the forecaster cannot simply
  invert the model. They are still our guesses at reality.
- Health labels are only as good as the simulated "efficiency". A real failure mode outside it (refrigerant
  leak, a stuck relay) is what the anomaly signal in P17 is for.
- The pipeline is built to **retrain on live data**: `python -m data.export_live --db <coldchain.db>` writes
  the backend's real readings in this same schema (without the truth columns, which only a simulator has).
